entry.title: 52,068 SonarQube pages on 9000, 12,052 fingerprints, and the tokens that sit in the project settings
entry.summary:
52,068 SonarQube pages on 9000, 12,052 fingerprints, and the tokens that sit in the project settings
SonarQube is a code analysis platform. Teams connect it to a source repository, it pulls the code, analyses it and reports on quality and security findings. To do that it stores credentials: repository tokens, CI webhook secrets, and in many installs the integration tokens that let the pipeline push analysis results. Requested from ZoomEye through the vendor SDK on 26 October 2026, one record per query, scope all asset types. Totals only. port=9000 && service="http" | 7,869,772 | port=9000 && title="SonarQube" | 52,068 | app="SonarQube" | 12,052 | app="SonarQube" && country="US" | 3,948 | title="SonarQube" && country="US" | 36,298 | The platform holds the analysis results for every project it scans, which is a list of every known weakness in the organisation's source code with file and line references. It is a map of where to look, and more useful to an attacker than a generic version fingerprint. Confirm the instance is reachable only from the network that runs the analysis and the developers who read the results. A public instance is a design decision worth recording, and most estates find at least one that nobody intended. The counts describe pages and fingerprints observed on one day, and a SonarQube behind an SSO proxy that returns a generic redirect will appear in neither. The numbers do not establish that authentication is weak, only that the interface is answering. Regional splits follow address geolocation. SonarQube documentation, security and authentication: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/latest/instance-administration/security/
SonarQube documentation, user tokens: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/latest/user-guide/user-tokens/

entry.title: Sviluppo API REST in PHP: quando serve e come si struttura
entry.summary:
Quando serve un'API REST
Un'API REST diventa necessaria quando il backend deve servire più client: un'app mobile, un frontend separato (SPA React, Vue, Angular), un gestionale di terze parti o un'integrazione con servizi esterni. Invece di duplicare la logica di business in ogni client, un'API centralizza dati e regole in un unico punto di accesso, garantendo coerenza e riducendo drasticamente la manutenzione. In PHP moderno, costruire un'API REST è un'operazione naturale: controller dedicati con single responsibility, middleware per autenticazione e rate limiting, risposte JSON strutturate con codici HTTP semantici, e validazione degli input con regole chiare e messaggi di errore utili.
